items.t: The condo-relevant point, framed strictly from verified sources: what a buyer or seller submits through this site's forms is personal information (information about identifiable individuals such as name, account numbers and photographs, including information about customers, per the OIPC guidance excerpt read pass). The live policy's own statements about such submissions are the inventory: registration-form information is used to send information about products and services to consenting parties, and personal information will not be disclosed to third parties without consent except in the page's stated legal-action / legal-requirement exceptions. The page does NOT state, for any specific current form (contact, home evaluation, guide request, listing alert), the purpose of collection, the retention period, the destruction practice, any service-provider or cross-border storage detail, or a breach-notification practice — each is absent from the page and not verified as current practice.

Governing framework (Province of BC, via search-result read pass): to collect, use or disclose personal information, private sector organizations in BC must follow the personal information and privacy rules set out in the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA), which are based on the 10 principles of privacy protection, and the rules generally apply to all private sector organizations including corporations, partnerships, unincorporated associations and not-for-profit organizations.

Privacy officer and policy duties (Province of BC, via search-result read): every organization must designate at least one privacy officer to oversee privacy practices and ensure compliance with PIPA, with the privacy officer as the primary contact for privacy-related questions and complaints; every organization must have a privacy policy, available upon request, that explains how personal information is collected, used, disclosed, stored and disposed of; and an organization is responsible for all personal information it handles, including information shared with contractors.

Oversight, safeguards and breaches (OIPC, via search-result read): organizations in BC are subject to PIPA, which has rules for how and when organizations can collect, use and/or disclose personal information; organizations also need to make reasonable security arrangements to protect personal information; and the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner (OIPC) for BC oversees and enforces the administration of PIPA, including investigating privacy complaints and whether organizations have reasonable safeguards. When personal information is collected, used, disclosed or destroyed in contravention of PIPA it is called a privacy breach; the OIPC guidance sets out a four-step breach response (containment, risk evaluation, notification, prevention) and organizations can report breaches to the OIPC.

The policy names no law at all. Neither BC's Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) nor the federal PIPEDA is mentioned anywhere in the text read — a visitor cannot tell from the page which statute the policy was drafted under, and that basis is not verified.

There is no privacy officer and no date on the page. The policy names no privacy officer or other designated contact person (questions are directed to "me/us" and to the Contact Page generally), and it states no effective date or last-updated date — the date the current text was adopted is not verified. The Province's frame expects a designated privacy officer and a policy explaining collection, use, disclosure, storage and disposal; the gap is a rebuild drafting item, not a fact about current practice.

Retention, disposal and breach practice are absent from the page. The live policy states no retention period, no destruction practice, no breach-notification practice and no service-provider or cross-border storage detail anywhere in the text read — those topics are absent from the page, which is a rebuild gap rather than a page statement; current practice on each is not verified.

faq.q: What does the site's privacy policy actually say?
faq.a: As page statements: that personal information will not be disclosed to third parties without the user's consent, with exceptions where disclosure is believed necessary for legal action over injury or interference or where the law is believed to require it; that aggregate audience information may be shared with advertisers, business partners and sponsors; that IP addresses and cookies are used for administration, preferences and trend tracking; and that users can opt out of directory sharing and marketing communications by email request.

faq.q: Which privacy law governs a BC realtor's website?
faq.a: The Province of BC states that private sector organizations in BC must follow the Personal Information Protection Act (PIPA) to collect, use or disclose personal information, under the oversight of the Office of the Information and Privacy Commissioner for BC — the live policy page itself names no statute, so that answer comes from the Province frame in, not from the page.

faq.q: Who do I contact about privacy on this site, according to the policy?
faq.a: The policy directs questions, concerns or complaints by email or phone using the contact information on the site's Contact Page, and names no individual privacy officer; the Province's compliance frame expects every organization to designate at least one privacy officer as the primary contact for privacy questions and complaints.

faq.q: Does the site use cookies, according to the policy?
faq.a: The policy says yes — cookies are used to specify unique preferences and to track user trends and patterns, are not used to gather a person's name or email address, and can be disabled through browser preferences. Whether that description matches the site's actual analytics configuration is not verified — no analytics or form-configuration source was opened pass.

faq.q: What happens to information I submit through a site form, according to the policy?
faq.a: The policy's registration-form statement, as a page statement: information from registration forms is used to send information about products and services to consenting parties, and personal information such as name, email and address is requested when a user registers as a member. The policy states no retention period, destruction practice or form-by-form purpose for the current site's lead forms — current practice on each is not verified.

The policy says yes, as a page statement — cookies are used to specify unique preferences and to track user trends and patterns, are not used to gather a person's name or email address, and can be disabled through browser preferences.

The policy says it may change from time to time, recommends visitors re-visit the page on occasion to learn of new practices, and states that continued use of the site after changes are posted means the user accepts those changes — all as page statements.

faq.q: What happens if there is a privacy breach?
faq.a: The policy itself states no breach-notification practice.
